summary_paragraph: A woman with a history of kidney and pancreas transplants, diastolic heart failure, and recurrent infections was admitted for acute heart failure exacerbation with bilateral pleural effusions and dyspnea. She was found to have a yeast urinary tract infection contributing to delirium, treated with IV fluconazole. During her stay, she developed transient atrial fibrillation attributed to volume overload, which resolved with diuresis. A cardiac catheterization revealed significant three-vessel coronary disease, but surgical intervention was deferred due to her complex medical status. She developed a right upper extremity DVT related to her PICC line, requiring anticoagulation with warfarin. Her immunosuppressants were adjusted due to acute kidney injury, which peaked post-catheterization but stabilized. She completed treatment for C. diff prophylaxis, and her mental status improved as metabolic and infectious factors resolved. She was transitioned from IV to oral diuresis with torsemide, and multiple medications were reconciled at discharge, including starting warfarin, metoprolol, and high-dose aspirin while discontinuing several others. She was discharged to extended care with stable vital signs and a plan for close outpatient follow-up.
problems: Acute on chronic combined systolic and diastolic heart failure
Acute venous embolism and thrombosis of superficial veins of upper extremity
Intestinal infection due to Clostridium difficile
